title: esQueranto: Differentiable Structured Quantum Light for Automated Scientific Discovery
authors: Marcello Armezzani, Tareq Jaouni, Pontus Lindgren, Sören Arlt, Mario Krenn, Xuemei Gu
abstract: Uncovering new phenomena in nature requires experiments. For centuries, their design has been exclusively a human endeavor. Today, a new paradigm is emerging in which artificial intelligence and computational methods can design experiments themselves. Realizing this form of automated scientific discovery requires simulators that are sufficiently expressive to represent the diverse physical processes and couplings from which new experiments can be constructed. In this direction, we introduce \textsc{esQueranto}, a differentiable software that brings photon-number quantum optics and structured-light propagation into a common description, allowing the spatial evolution of light to directly influence non-classical quantum states and their interference. \textsc{esQueranto} is implemented in JAX, providing automatic differentiation and hardware-accelerated evaluation for optimization and automated search. We demonstrate the framework across a broad range of quantum-optical applications that exercise complementary aspects of its physical description. By combining quantum and structured-light physics within a single differentiable simulator, \textsc{esQueranto} takes an important step towards the dream of a foundational simulator in physics.
summary: This paper introduces esQueranto, a novel, differentiable software framework designed to simulate complex quantum-optical experiments. It unifies disparate physical descriptions, such as structured light propagation and photon-number quantum optics, into a single, optimizable simulator. This advancement significantly accelerates the process of automated scientific discovery in quantum physics.
main_problem: The primary goal is to enable automated scientific discovery in quantum optics by creating a simulator capable of designing and simulating complex quantum-optical experiments.
main_result: The authors introduce esQueranto, a differentiable simulator that unifies photon-number quantum optics and structured-light propagation into a single framework.
method: The framework uses JAX for automatic differentiation, allowing optimization and automated search over physical parameters by modeling the evolution of quantum states through defined optical circuits.
model_or_system: The system models quantum-optical experiments involving photon-number states (Fock basis) and structured light (Laguerre-Gaussian modes). It incorporates elements like beam splitters, squeezing, photon loss, and dephasing.
key_observables: Fidelity, heralding probability, and the final quantum state $|\psiangle$ or density matrix $ho$.
important_parameters: Photon number cutoff ($N$), squeezing parameters ($r, \phi$), loss efficiency ($\eta$), and dephasing factor ($\xi$).
main_assumptions: The framework assumes that complex quantum-optical processes can be described by a sequence of differentiable transformations acting on the quantum state.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the combination of physical capabilities into a shared design space; Figure 8 shows the CPU-GPU scaling for batched optimization; Figure 9 tracks the loss evolution during NOON8 optimization.
paper_structure: The paper introduces esQueranto, details its unified physical description (state representation, optical elements, noise), and demonstrates its utility across multiple complex quantum-optical applications, including interferometry and state heralding.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, differentiable tool to explore the parameter space of quantum optical circuits, which is crucial for designing novel quantum information protocols and understanding open quantum systems.
